b71.why: 'his luck ended': Lustig creeps in hunched with finger to lips (the 'about to be caught' pose, its only use in the closing acts) clutching fake notes; a locked-off hold = the trap is already set and waiting
'The Secret Service caught him, with counterfeit money': agent slides in from the right, cuffs drop on Lustig, fake notes scatter at his feet; flash = the bust

b72.why: 'escaped from a New York jail, using a rope made from bedsheets': he edges toward the barred window with the knotted sheets; camera pans with him to the escape route
'He escaped': free again, mid-stride with his case, he hurries left across the street and the camera pans left with him - straight toward the agent who pops up on that side next
'Then he was caught again': the agent pops up from the LEFT this time, blocking the run he just made; cuffs drop again and a hard push + shake lands the reversal

b73.why: 'sent to Alcatraz': small, slumped prisoner on the dock while the camera pulls back to reveal the rock and the cold bay - the stage shrinks around him
'a prison hospital in Missouri, where he died of pneumonia': gaunt Lustig propped in an iron bed, nothing else in frame; a barely-moving drift = the quiet end, no prop, no flourish

b74.why: 'His death certificate lists his occupation': a clerk slides in, chin-in-hand, peering doubtfully at the form that drops on the desk; push toward the paper

x28.why: 'The man who had sold the most famous building in the world': lone suitcase-man walks away from the misty tower in the rain while the camera pulls back and he shrinks - a salesman with nothing left to sell

x29.why: 'No money. No title.': open-palmed shrug with empty white gloves, a last coin falls out of frame; gentle drift because the line is a sigh, not a slam
'Just a tidy number on a form': the form rises big and centre while Lustig stands small and composed at the edge; strong push makes the paper outweigh the man

b75.caption: So what was the sentence?
b75.why: 'So what was the sentence?': back at the tower where it began, Lustig walks in and raises one finger - the key point is coming; a still hold leaves the question hanging

b76.why: 'Give people a reason to feel special, and they will help you fool them': Lustig's open-palm offer, the mark grinning over his own cash; pan carries us from the flattery to the payment

'help you fool them': under the lit tower Lustig steps toward us with his hand out, inviting the handshake that makes the mark his helper; pull widens so the offer sits small against the tower he sold

b77.why: 'The tower never moved': slow pan right onto the real tower standing exactly where it always was, a Parisian reads the old scandal in the paper at left
'The man who sold it only borrowed a little of our oldest weakness': Lustig stands at the foot of the tower with an innocent shrug - only borrowed; camera pulls wide so the tower outlasts him

b78.why: 'If this story surprised you': Lustig strides back into the sunset plaza where the hook began and turns his finger on the viewer; push in, coin flips up - we are the next mark

'tell me which part of the con you would have fallen for': Lustig walks out of the hotel door heading left, open palm pitching again, and a tiny tower rises between him and a doubtful chin-in-hand mark; pan left follows his walk - the comments are his next pitch
